requirements.text: If it's failing, take the hardware out of service (server with serial SRV-WEB-102)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_011' AND serial_number = 'SRV-WEB-102' AND name = 'Linux-Web-02 (Apache)' AND status = 'maintenance' AND owner_id = 'USER_041' AND location_id = 'LOC_001' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: serial SRV-WEB-102 is CI_011 on the seed (one row)
the server is taken to be failing, as the benchmark assumes; the request's 'if' is resolved by the agent's investigation, which the final state cannot show
'out of service' is status = maintenance, not retired: the request then links this server to an active incident, which policy 5.1 allows only for in_use or maintenance CIs
name, owner_id, location_id and org_id kept from the benchmark check as unchanged seed values; not fixed by request or policy
the benchmark's updated_on > created_on predicate dropped: a server-kept timestamp, never a cell

requirements.text: find our primary major site outage incident and ensure this specific server is linked as an affected component
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE incident_affected_cis_id = 'TASKCI_015' AND configuration_item = 'CI_011' AND incident_id = 'INC_001' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (TASKCI_015 after TASKCI_014); the only link the task creates

the primary major site outage incident is INC_001 'MAJOR:SAP Database Unreachable': the only MAJOR-labelled incident, critical, in_progress, in the acting user's ORG_001; the only other critical ORG_001 incident, INC_057 'HR DB', says nothing of an outage
org_id follows the incident and the CI (both ORG_001)
the benchmark's created_on = updated_on predicate dropped: server-kept timestamps, never cells

requirements.text: ensure this specific server is linked as an affected component (exactly one link)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE configuration_item = 'CI_011' AND incident_id = 'INC_001' AND org_id = 'ORG_001'
assumptions: the natural-key form of the link: 'ensure ... is linked' means one link, no duplicates (the table's unique constraint on org, incident and CI also forbids a second)

requirements.text: server with serial SRV-WEB-102 (boundary: the near-matching SRV-WEB-101 stays in use)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_010' AND serial_number = 'SRV-WEB-101' AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: CI_010 'Linux-Web-01 (Apache)' differs from the target by one digit of serial and is the host the seed's disk incident INC_053 already links to; it must keep its seed status

requirements.text: this specific server is linked (boundary: the near-matching SRV-WEB-101 is not linked to the outage incident)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE configuration_item = 'CI_010' AND incident_id = 'INC_001'
assumptions: no link between CI_010 and INC_001 exists on the seed and none must be created

requirements.text: find our primary major site outage incident (boundary: the server is linked to no other incident)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE configuration_item = 'CI_011' AND incident_id <> 'INC_001'
assumptions: a loose reading of 'major site outage' could pick another critical incident (INC_057 'HR DB' in ORG_001, or the disk incidents INC_030 and INC_053); CI_011 has no links on the seed and must gain only the INC_001 one

ci_011_status_update_to_maintenance_veri.evidence: its cells (serial, name, status maintenance, owner, location, org) are carried by the CI_011 requirement; the predicate updated_on > created_on tests server-kept timestamps and is dropped

ci_011_to_inc_001_link_creation_verifier.evidence: its cells (TASKCI_015 linking CI_011 to INC_001 in ORG_001) are carried by the link requirement; the predicate created_on = updated_on tests server-kept timestamps and is dropped

complete_workflow_state_verifier.evidence: a UNION ALL composite of the CI_011 status check and the TASKCI_015 link check, carried jointly by those two requirements (named in their source); its updated_on > created_on predicate tests server-kept timestamps and is dropped, as in the status check

notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that the near-matching CI_010 (serial SRV-WEB-101) is not linked to INC_001; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because the near-matching serial is the boundary of the request's selector, and an agent that links both web hosts would pass the anchored TASKCI_015 requirement while only this stay catches the extra link.
disagreement: disposition: 'complete_workflow_state_verifier': excluded in one pass as a composite of the status and link checks, kept in the other; chose repaired, carried jointly by the CI_011 status requirement and the TASKCI_015 link requirement (named in their source), because a composite over cells other carried checks test is carried, not excluded, and its timestamp predicate is dropped like the status check's.
disagreement: form: the stay that CI_011 links to no incident but INC_001 repeats its selector's columns in cells in one pass and has empty cells in the other, with identical sql; chose empty cells, since a column the selector fixes is not repeated.
Both passes kept the status check and the link check whole; they are recorded as repaired because each tests a server-kept timestamp (updated_on > created_on, created_on = updated_on) that is dropped from the requirement. Both passes repeated the selector's columns in the cells of the natural-key link requirement; those cells are removed, as the selector already fixes them.
The first sentence ('Investigate the records ... check if it aligns with the symptoms') is read-only and leaves no database requirement. The seed's disk incidents link to the first web host CI_010, not CI_011, so the investigation's answer is not visible in the data; the request's framing ('a repeat of the disk failures on the second web host') and the benchmark's checks take the server as failing.
